messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 - spike in 5xx and latency starting ~1719532000. Smart-routing fallback is triggering cross-region failover and we're seeing request duplication. Alert: https://ops.redwood.internal/alerts/INC-9812 :rotating_light:

alice (oncall): on it. paging ben + carla. assigning PD to ben now.

ben (sre): ack. seeing error rate ~12% on /v1/generate from region-eu and sudden CPU spikes on region-us replicas. graphs: p95 latency doubled, outgoing request count to us replicas ~= incoming * 2.

carla (plat-lead): hypothesis: failover policy is misconfigured to fanout to multiple compatible variants/regions instead of single fallback. combined with aggressive client retry policy -> thundering herd. any recent policy deploys?

frank (eng): I pushed a routing-policy tweak yesterday (experiment: multi-variant fallback) to reduce model mismatch errors. might be related.

ben (sre): logs show client retry headers like `Retry-After: 0` and exponential retries for 429/503. clients retry immediately -> our smart-routing fires failover to region-us; because of the policy change, it also sends to a variant in us-ssd, effectively doubling attempts.

eric (infra): scaling is reacting but slower. we temporarily hit admission limits on the us pool and started rejecting, which fed back to clients -> more retries.

alice (oncall): impact? which customers affected? devon can you pull support queue and customer-facing signals?

devon (customer-success): seeing 8 open tickets referencing "slow responses" and 2 on L3 customers reporting degraded throughput for embeddings. letting sales know. preparing customer comms draft.

ben (sre): immediate mitigation plan: 1) rollback last routing-policy experiment (disable multi-variant fanout) 2) apply a short ephem rate-limit on cross-region failover traffic 3) instruct clients to honor Retry-After and set recommended jitter/backoff.

carla (plat-lead): agree. frank can you revert the policy flag quickly? If we can't revert, apply a patch to change fallback_mode -> single_hop.

frank (eng): doing revert now. CLI: `curl -X PATCH https://console.redwood.internal/api/policies/route-983 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"fallback_mode":"single_hop","fanout":false}'`


deploy-bot: routing-policy route-983: change applied by frank at 1719532224.

ben (sre): applying transient rate-limit on proxy: `rlimit set --route /v1/generate --match header:X-Region-Fallback --rate 200r/s`

eric (infra): rate limit in place and we bumped us replica admission to +20% to absorb steady-state.

alice (oncall): ben, can you confirm whether duplicates stopped?

ben (sre): metrics: outgoing requests to us replicas now approx equal incoming. 5xx rate falling from 12% -> 1.8% in last 3m. latency trending down. marking as mitigated. :white_check_mark:

devon (customer-success): sending provisional customer note: "We've mitigated an incident causing increased latency and errors for some requests. Root cause: routing policy change combined with aggressive client retries. We'll follow up with permanent fixes and recommended client backoff guidance."

carla (plat-lead): please open follow-up tickets: - postmortem (owner: ben) - client-backoff doc update (owner: frank) - routing-policy safe-deploy checks (owner: carla) - customer RCA + comms (owner: devon)

frank (eng): creating PR to add a gating test to policy deploys to detect fanout configs. snippet I ran locally that triggered the issue: ```json
{
  "id":"route-983",
  "fallback_mode":"multi_variant",
  "fanout": true,
  "compatible_variants":["gpt-medium","gpt-quant-lite"]
}
```

ben (sre): note for postmortem: interplay of client retry loops + policy fanout = traffic amplification. mitigation effective but temporary. we should add server-side dedup or prefer single-hop fallback by default.

alice (oncall): closing incident channel. will handover to ben/carla for postmortem. thanks all.

incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-9812 status -> mitigated at 1719532487. PagerDuty: resolved.
